fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled pattern string pointer xs is dereferenced at index 0 to compute the SWAR first-byte mask.
Pattern's last byte xs[m-1] is read; m is the pattern length supplied by the caller.
Pointer s1 is set to ys+m-1, pointing near the end of the haystack for the last-byte comparison.
Loop limit is computed as n-m-sizeof(bitint); if n-m is smaller than sizeof(bitint), lim becomes negative and the SWAR loop is skipped.
SWAR loop iterates over the haystack in sizeof(bitint) chunks; each iteration reads sizeof(bitint) bytes from s0+i and s1+i.
Reads sizeof(bitint) bytes from haystack at offset i; this is within bounds because i < lim = n-m-sizeof(bitint).
Reads sizeof(bitint) bytes from s1+i = ys+m-1+i; since i < n-m-sizeof(bitint), the read ends at ys+n-1, within bounds.
Combines first-byte and last-byte equality checks into a single bitmask.
Computes a bitmask of candidate positions where both first and last bytes match.
Iterates over each candidate byte position within the current SWAR chunk.
Candidate match offset idx is computed as the chunk base plus the byte position within the chunk.
Pointer p points to the byte after the candidate first-byte match in the haystack.

memcmp reads m-2 bytes starting at p = ys+idx+1; when idx is near the end of the haystack (idx close to n-m), this read can extend past the end of the allocated buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow read.
mrb_memsearch dispatches to memsearch_swar for patterns of length >= 2, passing the attacker-controlled pattern and haystack lengths.
mrb_str_index calls mrb_memsearch with the substring pattern and the haystack slice starting at the offset.
